name: Tell a Friend
description: Say what the talk is about the way you would across a table, and keep the best accidental lines.
key_questions: What is this talk about, in your words, right now?|What did you just say that surprised you?|Which line would you repeat to someone tomorrow?

name: What Everyone Gets Wrong
description: Find the belief the audience walks in with that the talk overturns.
key_questions: What does this room believe today?|Where is that belief wrong, or incomplete?|What story proves it?

name: The One Thing
description: Pick the single idea people should repeat on the way out.
key_questions: If they remember one sentence, what is it?|Could someone repeat it without you there?|Which part of the talk serves it least?

name: Open a Loop
description: Plant a question early that the talk only answers near the end.
key_questions: What question can you raise in the first minute?|What would make them need the answer?|Where exactly does it close?

name: The Prop or the Moment
description: Find the physical object, demo, or visual moment that makes the idea impossible to forget.
key_questions: What could you hold up, show, or do on stage?|What should they actually see when the key idea lands?|Would the talk survive without it?

name: Cold Open Three Ways
description: Draft three openings, a scene, a number, and a question, and say each aloud.
key_questions: Which opening makes you lean in?|Which one sounds like you?|Which one does the rest of the talk pay off?

name: The Heckler
description: Name the sharpest skeptic in the room and answer them inside the talk.
key_questions: Who in the audience doubts this most?|What is their best objection?|Where in the talk do you answer it before they ask?

name: Cut a Minute
description: Find the minute the talk could lose without anyone missing it.
key_questions: Which part do you rush when you rehearse?|Which part do you enjoy more than they will?|What happens if it is gone?
